Subject: Private endpoint network checklist — initial questions

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Our security team asked me to gather concrete guidance on what we need to open from our on-prem environment to support a Redwood private connector (VPC peering / private endpoint). I attached our current network request template and a short list of existing egress controls.

Quick questions to start:
- Which IP ranges or FQDNs should be allowlisted for control-plane traffic vs model-serving data plane?
- Do you require any inbound rules into our network, or is the connector always outbound?
- Any recommended approach for customers that route all outbound through an HTTP proxy?

We need this to complete our change control packet for our infra team. I can loop in our cloud networking lead if helpful.

From: jordan_blake@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Private endpoint network checklist — initial questions

Claire — thanks for the clear list and the attachment. Looping Marcus (network ops) and Kimberly (private deployments) to validate a short runbook.

High level answers up front: the private connector is outbound-only from your VPC/on‑prem to Redwood — no inbound firewall holes required. There are two logical egress buckets you should allowlist:

1) Control plane (TLS to our control plane for lifecycle events, health, rollouts)
   - Domain: controlplane.redwood-inference.com
   - Ports: TCP 443
   - IP guidance: we publish a stable set of NAT egress IPs (see attachment) but we can also support FQDN allowlisting if your proxy supports TLS SNI.

2) Data plane (model serving; streaming token traffic may go to dedicated model nodes)
   - Domain: models-us.redwood-inference.com (region-specific hostnames)
   - Ports: TCP 443 and optional TCP 443+ for websocket/streaming upgrades
   - Recommendation: prefer FQDN allowlist + certificate validation. If you require IPs, use the static NAT IP list we provide for the customer: 34.210.112.0/24, 52.14.64.0/25 (we'll emit exact CIDRs per customer contract).

Proxy note: if you route all outbound via an HTTP proxy, we support CONNECT proxying for TLS and can provide the SNI and certificate pins to allow traffic through without intercepting TLS. If your proxy performs TLS interception, we recommend a dedicated proxy path that preserves certificate validation for Redwood endpoints or using a mutual-TLS option (can provide certs).

I've attached a preliminary checklist (redwood_private_endpoint_checklist.xlsx) with the fields our ops team needs in the RFC. Marcus / Kimberly — can you confirm the static IP sets and whether we should recommend NAT Gateway vs egress-proxy in the runbook?

Next step: propose a 30-minute alignment call Friday to finalize allowlist entries and the change window.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: Private endpoint network checklist — internal runbook draft

Team — forwarding Claire's note. Draft runbook items below; please add corrections inline. I'm trying to keep the customer-facing doc as prescriptive as possible so their change control reviewers can copy/paste.

-- BEGIN DRAFT RUNBOOK --
Purpose: capture minimal firewall/egress policy required for EdgeWorks private connector (on-prem).

A) Mode of connectivity
- Outbound-only connections from customer network to Redwood control plane and model endpoints. No inbound NAT required.

B) Allowlist strategy (preferred order)
- 1) FQDN-based allowlist: controlplane.redwood-inference.com, models-us.redwood-inference.com. Require TLS SNI passthrough on proxies.
- 2) Static egress IPs (for environments that cannot allowlist FQDNs). Provide per-customer NAT IP list; recommended CIDRs (examples): 34.210.112.0/24, 52.14.64.0/25.
- 3) Service tags: where cloud provider supports tags for outbound, recommend mapping to our published service tag set.

C) Firewall rules (minimum)
- Allow outbound TCP 443 to controlplane.redwood-inference.com (SNI: controlplane.redwood-inference.com)
- Allow outbound TCP 443 to models-us.redwood-inference.com (support websocket upgrade: Connection: Upgrade)
- Allow DNS (UDP 53/TCP 53) to resolve Redwood hostnames from your DNS resolvers.
- Allow NTP (UDP 123) if your HA checks rely on accurate time.

D) Proxying & TLS inspection
- If HTTP CONNECT is used, ensure CONNECT is allowed to our FQDNs and that proxies do not terminate TLS for requests to Redwood unless mutual-TLS is in place.

E) Health & monitoring checks
- Allow outbound to health.redwood-inference.com for probe polling (TCP 443).
- Recommend egress flow logs for 72 hours to validate behavior during cutover.

F) Exceptions / escalation
- If customer must route via corporate egress appliance that filters by IP only, we'll provide a signed list of NAT IPs and a change control template.

-- END DRAFT RUNBOOK --

Marcus / Kimberly: please add any missing ports (we discussed metrics ingestion earlier) and confirm whether the example CIDRs above are okay to include in a customer RFC or if legal requires pseudonyms.

Thanks,
Jordan
From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: jordan_blake@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 11:46:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private endpoint network checklist — internal runbook draft

Jordan — looks good. A few suggested edits before we hand to EdgeWorks: 

- Replace example CIDRs with the canonical per-customer NAT block placeholder (e.g., <REDACTED_CUSTOMER_NAT_BLOCKS>) and attach the signed IP roster in a separate secure doc. Security teams prefer not seeing operational CIDRs in initial RFCs.
- Add metrics/telemetry endpoints: allow outbound TCP 443 to traces.redwood-inference.com and metrics.redwood-inference.com (TLS). These are small, outbound-only flows for diagnostics.
- Note about long-lived WebSocket streams: recommend idle-timeouts on corporate proxies >= 10 minutes, and allow large POST bodies for streaming initial requests.
- For on-prem offices that must use a forced egress proxy, recommend a dedicated proxy route that bypasses corporate inspection for Redwood endpoints OR deploy our proxy-aware mutual-TLS option.

I'll draft the short snippet for the change control packet that clarifies: no inbound firewall openings, provide per-customer IP roster during the maintenance window, and request 5 minutes of packet capture after initial cutover for validation.

Marcus Lin
Network Operations, Redwood Inference

Claire — thanks again. Summary and next steps below (short runbook + ask).

Summary (what EdgeWorks needs to do):
- Allow outbound TLS (TCP 443) to controlplane.redwood-inference.com and models-us.redwood-inference.com (preferred: FQDN/SNI).
- Allow DNS and NTP as noted.
- If you require IP-only allowlisting, we'll deliver a signed per-customer NAT IP roster in a separate secure attachment.
- For proxyed environments: enable HTTP CONNECT for the Redwood FQDNs or provision a proxy path that preserves certificate validation. If TLS interception is unavoidable, request our mutual-TLS option and we'll provide certs.

Attachments included: redwood_private_endpoint_checklist.xlsx (checklist for your RFC), and we will share the signed IP roster after we confirm the maintenance window.

Proposed next steps:
1) Can you share EdgeWorks change-control owner and an available 30-minute slot next week?
2) If you prefer, I can provide a prefilled RFC with placeholders (NAT block, maintenance window) for your infra team to submit.

Thanks — happy to hop on a call to walk the runbook with your reviewers.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
